     1	# snapshot toolchain
     2	
     3	Three small scripts plus a shared library that take periodic compressed
     4	snapshots of a directory, replicate them off-host, and rotate old ones out.
     5	
     6	    lib/common.sh    logging, config loading, staging, space check, replication
     7	    snapshot.sh      makes one archive, replicates it, prints one manifest record
     8	    prune.sh         reads manifest records, rotates old archives out
     9	    run-backup.sh    runs snapshot.sh, feeds its manifest to prune.sh
    10	
    11	## Usage
    12	
    13	    ./run-backup.sh --label nightly --config /etc/backup.conf [--force]
    14	
    15	`run-backup.sh` is the only entry point cron needs. `snapshot.sh` and
    16	`prune.sh` are usable on their own, which is why each one loads its own
    17	config and validates its own inputs instead of trusting the caller.
    18	
    19	`--force` (or `BACKUP_FORCE=1`) downgrades the pre-flight free-space check
    20	from fatal to a warning. Use it when you know the archive filesystem has
    21	room that `df` cannot see, e.g. because a large archive is about to rotate
    22	out on the same run.
    23	
    24	## Config file
    25	
    26	`load_config` reads `KEY=VALUE` lines and exports only keys beginning with
    27	`BACKUP_`; anything else is logged and skipped so a typo in the config
    28	cannot clobber `PATH`. Recognised keys:
    29	
    30	    BACKUP_SOURCE_DIR    directory to snapshot            (required)
    31	    BACKUP_ARCHIVE_DIR   where archives are written       (required)
    32	    BACKUP_KEEP          archives kept per label          (default 5)
    33	    BACKUP_REMOTE        user@host of the replica         (optional)
    34	    BACKUP_REMOTE_DIR    directory on the replica         (required with the above)
    35	    BACKUP_FORCE         1 to pre-set --force             (optional)
    36	
    37	## Manifest format (v2)
    38	
    39	`snapshot.sh` writes exactly one tab-separated record to stdout:
    40	
    41	    <label>\t<epoch>\t<bytes>\t<archive-path>
    42	
    43	v1 records had no label column; the label had to be recovered from the
    44	archive filename, which stopped working the moment a label contained a `-`.
    45

    48	made from what is actually on disk, so a stale manifest can never delete
    49	an archive that a later run created.
    50	
    51	## Exit status
    52	
    53	`snapshot.sh` exits 3 when the source tree is empty and nothing was
    54	written. `run-backup.sh` treats that as success and skips rotation, so a
    55	host that has not produced any data yet cannot rotate its last good
    56	archive out from under itself.
    57	
    58	## Archive naming
    59	
    60	    <archive-dir>/<label>-<UTC timestamp>.tar.gz

The manifest format change universally disables pruning, and the default force handling disables the principal disk-safety feature. Replication also has atomicity, cleanup, command-injection, and permission problems that can leave corrupt backups, leak data, or exhaust storage.
